## Terminology

This project uses a small set of terms consistently. A few of them, such as "verified" and
"harness", carry a narrower meaning here than in general use.

Signed Instruction Block
: An instruction in plain text followed by a detached signature over it. The instruction is what
  a person reads and what the signature covers; there is no second, encoded copy. Shortened to
  "block" once the context is clear.

Instruction
: The text a human signed. It is written in natural language and does not encode permissions; a
  classifier decides what it authorizes.

Signer
: The named human who signed a block, identified by a stable id such as `alice@example.com`
  (the `iss` header field). The only source of authority in the design.

Key Identifier
: The name of the key a signer used, of the form `signer#label` (the `kid` field). A signer can
  hold several keys, such as a dev key and a passkey, and rotate them independently.

Audience
: The deployment or harness a block is meant for (the `aud` field). A block whose audience does
  not match the harness confers nothing there.

Canonicalization Rule
: The named, versioned transformation applied to the instruction before signing and before
  verifying (the `canon` field), so that the same instruction verifies after a chat client has
  re-wrapped it or replaced its quotes.

Verifier
: The deterministic component in the harness that extracts every block from the agent's context,
  checks it, and produces the manifest. It contains no model and makes no allow or deny decision.

Verified
: The status of a block whose signature checks against an enrolled key and whose validity window,
  audience and metadata all hold. Only verified blocks carry authority. A block that fails is
  described by its status (`expired`, `invalid_signature` and so on), never as "invalid" alone.

Provenance Manifest
: The verifier's output: every block found in context, its status, its signer and text, and where
  in the context it came from. Everything not listed is unsigned.

Harness
: The runtime that executes an agent's tool calls, such as Claude Code or Codex. The verifier and
  the manifest channel run in the harness, outside the model loop.

Permission Classifier
: The model that decides whether a proposed tool call may run. It consumes the manifest as
  structured input. Claude Code's auto mode has one built in; the reference implementation also
  ships its own.

Gate
: The hook-side check that denies a policy-covered action when no verified block covers it. It is
  the guarantee; the classifier is the judgment.

Gated Action
: An action the gate policy names as requiring human authorization, such as a deploy. The policy
  is harness configuration and lives outside the repository.

Origin
: Where a block was found: the user's prompt, the project's instruction files, a tool result, or
  an assistant message. Origin labels tell the classifier who put the text in front of the agent.

Dev Mode
: The mode in which software keys on disk sign and verify blocks, with a warning on every
  operation. Blocks and keys marked `dev` confer nothing in enforced mode.

Enforced Mode
: The mode in which only hardware-backed, user-verified keys count. Available with the WebAuthn
  signing path in Phase 2.


## Concepts

A few ideas recur throughout the documentation and are easier to state once:

Authorship, not permission
: A block proves who wrote the text and when. Whether that text permits a specific action is a
  reading of natural language, and reading is the classifier's job.

Unsigned text confers nothing
: Runbooks, `CLAUDE.md`, commit messages, fetched pages, subagent reports and quoted chat threads
  can all say "deploys are pre-authorized". None of it is an instruction from a human unless it is
  inside a verified block.

Fail closed on authority
: When the verifier, the registry, the session store or the classifier fails, a gated action is
  denied and the reason names the failure. A non-gated action proceeds. The hook never relies on
  the harness's own default, which is to proceed.

Two channels to the classifier
: In Claude Code the manifest reaches the auto-mode classifier as a short note through the
  PostToolUse hook's `classifierContext` field, and the gate runs in the PreToolUse hook before the
  classifier is consulted. Either layer stops the injected-authorization attack on its own.
